audit.whatIsWrong: The win-rate sources disagree by twelve points: MC_WR_TABLES.sejuani.kennen is 51.88 over 133 games, the packet says 63.83 over 47 games. The page reads as a lane Sejuani survives, which suits 51.88 and understates 63.83.
audit.why: One number says a coin flip, the other says a strongly favoured lane. I cannot settle it from the data available, so no difficulty, rating or side changed and the question is recorded instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 are scored Kennen on win[3] and phases[3].side, but whys[3] ends 'you own this window' and mid opens 'Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely Sejuani's strongest window in this lane'. Separately, the stated reason for that window is wrong — see point 6.
audit.why: The caption and the side disagree outright, and here the underlying justification is also false, so fixing the side without fixing the reason would bake in a bad argument. I corrected the mechanical claim and left the side alone, because which way that stage should fall depends on the unresolved win rate.
audit.corrected: The false cooldown that justified the stage is fixed in whys[3], spikes[1] and mid; the side itself is deferred with the win-rate question.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says Kennen must 'hit five marks to proc his own stun' and late calls it a 'five-mark burst rotation'. Riot's Mark of the Storm text: 'Kennen stuns enemies he hits 3 times with his abilities.' It is three, not five. wants.foe[0] also calls Sejuani's resistances 'passive Permafrost resistances' — they come from Fury of the North, and Permafrost is her E stun.
audit.why: Three versus five is the difference between a stun that arrives after a shuriken, a W proc and a Lightning Rush pass — which is one ordinary rotation — and one that supposedly needs a long setup. A Sejuani counting to five walks into the stun on the third hit. Given that Slicing Maelstrom applies marks repeatedly to everything nearby, the three-hit threshold is also why standing in his ultimate chain-stuns rather than merely hurting.
audit.corrected: Three marks stated in wants.foe[2] and late; Fury of the North named correctly in wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] tells the player to 'track its 14-second cooldown' on Lightning Rush and mid repeats 'Lightning Rush sits on a 14-second cooldown'. whys[3] calls it 'a long cooldown' and rests Sejuani's ownership of levels 4-5 on that. Lightning Rush is 10/9/8/7/6 seconds.
audit.why: It is never 14 at any rank, and at levels 4-5 it is 9 or 8 seconds — one of the shortest repositioning tools in the lane, not a long one. The page tells a Sejuani that Kennen's escape is down for fourteen seconds when it is actually back in eight, which is precisely the kind of error that gets a player killed stepping up on a window that already closed. Slicing Maelstrom, by contrast, is a flat 120 seconds at every rank, and that is the number actually worth banking a fight around.
audit.corrected: Lightning Rush's real 10-to-6-second range replaces the 14 in whys[3], spikes[1], mid, breakdown.cooldowns and loading; Slicing Maelstrom's flat 120s is added as the cooldown that does gate his commits.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] and spikes[3] talk about tank items and resistances generically, and report[8] offers armour or magic resist 'by damage type' without saying which applies.
audit.why: Kennen is a magic-damage champion whose output scales with attack speed through Electrical Surge's on-hit marks, so armour does almost nothing here and magic resist does almost everything. Naming the damage type turns a generic itemisation line into an actionable one.
audit.corrected: Magic resist called out explicitly in spikes[3] and report[8].t.

edits.after: Kennen's mark-stun needs three separate hits and your Frost-loaded W-W-E stun fires faster and on demand — but Lightning Rush is only 9 seconds here, not fourteen, so the window closes sooner than it looks.

edits.after: Lightning Rush is his main harass here — he runs through you to stack marks. It is 10 seconds at rank 1 and 8 by rank 3, so step up on the pass, not after it.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are genuinely Sejuani's strongest window in this lane because Kennen's Lightning Rush sits on a 14-second cooldown and his mark-stacking pattern requires him to hit you three times before his own stun fires — keep your Frost-stacking W-W-E combo loaded and punish every reset attempt he makes on the wave. At level 6 the lane flips hard in your favour: Glacial Prison travels faster than Lightning Rush and creates a blizzard that Kennen cannot sprint out of, so drop R on his path, let the secondary slow-to-stun fire, and chain your E Permafrost on top — every subsequent gank becomes a guaranteed kill and Kennen is forced to respect the river or die.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Sejuani's best window in this lane, but not for the reason it looks: Lightning Rush is 10 seconds at rank 1 and only 8 by rank 3, so his escape is back fast and you must punish on the pass rather than wait it out. What does gate him is Mark of the Storm — he needs three hits before his own stun fires, so deny the third and the rotation is harmless. Keep the Frost-stacking W-W-E loaded and punish every reset on the wave. At level 6 the lane flips: Glacial Prison throws 1300 and drops a blizzard Kennen cannot sprint out of, so put R on his path and chain Permafrost on top. Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120 seconds — once it is spent, every gank is a kill.

edits.before: Two tank items make you essentially unkillable by Kennen alone — his five-mark burst rotation does meaningful damage to a squishy target but not to a Sunfire-Heartsteel Sejuani who is regenerating HP on contact with the wave, so he must draft his whole team around executing you, which means he cannot safely split. Your job in teamfights is to Arctic Assault the backline or Glacial Prison from range, E-stun every cluster he tries to Lightning Rush through, and let your team clean up; one well-placed R at a dragon or baron fight is worth every CS you lost in the early poke war.
edits.after: Two tank items make you essentially unkillable by Kennen alone — his three-mark burst rotation deletes squishies but not a Sunfire-and-Rookern Sejuani, so he has to draft his whole team around executing you and cannot safely split. Build magic resist rather than armour; every point of his damage is magic. In teamfights, Arctic Assault the backline or throw Glacial Prison from 1300, E-stun every cluster he tries to Lightning Rush through, and let your team clean up. One well-placed R at dragon is worth every CS you lost in the poke war.

edits.after: - Kennen Lightning Rush: 10s at rank 1 down to 6s, so it is back fast — punish on the pass. - Mark of the Storm stuns on the third hit: deny it. - Slicing Maelstrom is a flat 120s, the one worth banking against.

edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pots. First: Sunfire Aegis into Mercury's Treads; then Kaenic Rookern. All his damage is magic — skip the armour.

notes: Win-rate sources conflict (MC_WR_TABLES 51.88 over 133 games versus the packet's 63.83 over 47), so no side, rating or difficulty changed; every edit here is a mechanical correction that holds under either number. Levels 4-5 is scored Kennen while two fields call it Sejuani's best window — that needs re-siding once the win rate is settled. Deliberately not asserted: whether Mercury's Treads tenacity meaningfully shortens Mark of the Storm's stun, and whether Sejuani's Frost Armor slow immunity does anything against his kit. Riot's Kennen text lists no slow at all, so I made no slow-immunity claim on this page even though it is true elsewhere in the slice. kennen.json's needsResearch is empty, which the brief defines as unknown, so nothing about cleanse, QSS or tenacity is stated.
